relationship: Changing a prism's dimensions changes internal volume and exposed surface area through different linked geometric decompositions.

learnerLoop.action: Change the prism dimensions and account for the requested volume or surface terms.
learnerLoop.modelChange: The solid, its cross-section and unwrapped surface update.
learnerLoop.evidence: The 3D model, net and checked working show capacity and material consequences.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Choose which dimension or term to use to meet the next constraint.

invariants: Prism volume is cross-sectional area multiplied by length.
Surface area includes both end caps and every lengthwise face.
safeAdaptations: Vary valid prism dimensions and material or capacity targets.
Adjust working support while retaining linked solid and net evidence.
nonGoals: Counting only visible faces or treating surface area as volume.

task.description: Current prism design target, material budget or capacity constraint.
task.visibility: Shown for the current generated problem.

model.description: Prism dimensions and its unfolded surface/net update together.
model.visibility: Present throughout; geometry and net readouts change with the active handle or checked dimensions.

working.description: Ordered area, perimeter, length, side, volume and surface-area calculations.
working.visibility: Always present; dynamic inputs follow the selected working level and problem type.

evidence.description: Capacity and material readouts, solid/net state and checked working expose the trade-off.
evidence.visibility: Shown throughout and updated after geometry or working changes.

completion.description: Solved prism problem, next problem and working-level upgrade.
completion.visibility: Shown only when visual constraints and required working checks pass.

settings.description: Working support level and problem reset.
settings.visibility: Working buttons are shown for the current problem; higher levels unlock by solved count.

inputs.description: Problem-specific dimension handle and generated calculation fields.
inputs.visibility: A length handle is used for extrude and a width handle for reshape; fields are generated by level.

cross-section.description: Rectangular cross-section area A and perimeter P from width w and height h.
cross-section.domain: Square units for A; linear units for P.
cross-section.source: Current dimensions and generated A/P working entries.

length.description: Prism length L, the extrude dimension or the fixed invariant in reshape cases.
length.source: #lengthHandle in extrude or generated task dimensions.

volume.source: Cross-section area and length; extrude level-2 or reshape level-2 work may own the entry.

surface-terms.description: Lengthwise side area P × L, two end caps 2A and total surface area SA.
surface-terms.source: Dimensions and generated side/SA work entries.

modes.none: Source level 0 is labelled Off: drag the problem-specific dimension and use the shown calculation; at least two geometry moves are required.
modes.some: Source level 1 is labelled Some: extrude owns L; reshape owns SA, with the remaining relationship shown.
modes.all: Source level 2 is labelled All: extrude requires A, P, L, side and SA; reshape requires A, P, V, side and SA in the source's ordered chain.
modes.problem-types: Extrude targets capacity and a surface budget; reshape changes the cross-section while volume/length relationships remain part of the source checks.

dependencies: Visual success is type-specific: extrude requires target volume and surface area within budget; reshape requires surface area within budget.
At level 1/2, working keys are checked in dependency order: A/P precede downstream L/V/side/SA fields as defined by the problem type.
Changing geometry invalidates prior working values; the next card appears only after visualSuccess and workingOK pass.
#nextProblem advances from the completion card, while higher support is offered after the source's solved-count threshold.
implementation.completion: The source currentComplete/solved checks require the visual constraint and selected working-level fields; a successful state shows #nextCard with next-problem and upgrade actions.
limitations: Problem dimensions and target budgets are generated; dynamic answer inputs have stable data-answer keys but no separate per-problem IDs.
Reshape geometry uses source snap/target checks and a material inequality, so surface area is not required to equal a single fixed value.
